known_pitfall_claim: The asserted equality f[S₁ \ f⁻¹(H)] = S₂ \ H holds for the given continuous mapping without requiring surjectivity.
pitfall_counterexample: Let S₁={a} and S₂={b,c}, each with the discrete topology. Define f:S₁→S₂ by f(a)=b, and take H=∅. Every map between discrete spaces is continuous, so all stated hypotheses hold. The map is not surjective because c∉f[S₁].
